results.headline: You have 68 people worth calling.
results.lede: We pulled the entire Cambridge-area market for this profile and scored every one of them against the same rubric. Not a shortlist assembled from somebody's network. The whole market, measured the same way, ranked.
results.closing: The ten strongest are in section 02, each with the reasoning behind the score. The full 68 are in section 06. Every name carries a written case you can check against that person's own record.

featured_intro: The highest-scoring people in the market for this seat. Every one of them currently does a version of this job at a company that operates like yours. None of them is looking for a job, which is the entire point.

method.lede: Two questions carry 350 of the 400 available points: does this person's employer operate like yours, and have they actually done this job before? They are the two that predict whether somebody can walk in and do the work. Everything else is a tiebreaker.
method.dna_body: The strongest single predictor is what a candidate's current employer actually does. Not the industry label the company filed under, which is wrong often enough to be dangerous, but the real work: what they build, who pays for it, at what tolerance, and at what size. A scientist inside a 40,000-person pharma and a scientist at a twenty-five-person AI-for-biology startup can hold the same title and be doing entirely different jobs.
method.dna_axis: For this search we scored on operating shape rather than product category. A generative-design scientist at a small AI-for-materials company scores higher than an antibody specialist inside a large pharma, because at your size there is no platform team, no separate assay group, and nobody standing between the model and the molecule. That is the reality that has to transfer.
dna_tiers: Direct peers. Generate:Biomedicines, Dyno Therapeutics, Lila Sciences, Manifold Bio, Ai Proteins. Venture-backed, own both the model and the wet lab, revenue from pharma partnerships.
Strong overlap. Metaphore, Seismic Therapeutic, Ampersand Biomedicines. AI-first biologics design, adjacent modality or one stage further along.
Partial. Visterra, Tectonic, Valo Health, the Wyss Institute. Real AI-in-biology work, but on delivery, on small molecules, or in a purely academic setting.
Tangential. Computational drug discovery without generative design, or AI-for-science outside biologics.
No transfer. Materials, energy, defence R&D, consumer software.
method.role_body: The second question is what a candidate's current seat actually carries, inferred from their real employer rather than their title string. Titles in this market are close to meaningless. "Senior Scientist" and "Principal Scientist" are the two commonest strings in the entire pull, and neither one tells you whether the person has ever picked an epitope. We scored what somebody in that seat, at that company, actually does all day.
role_tiers: Already owns a design campaign end to end. Picks the target, runs the model, briefs the lab, reads the assay.
Owns the model work and works directly with a lab, but a program manager or a platform team sits in between.
Related function with a real gap in scope, level, or operating context.
Wrong function for this seat. Scored low rather than removed, because a wrong exclusion is invisible and permanent.
method.role_note: A level mismatch never disqualifies anyone. A staff scientist running a larger operation is a better candidate than a director running a smaller one, and postdocs in this field routinely carry eight years of the required work under a junior-sounding label.
method.rest_heading: The last 50 points, and the tiebreakers
method.rest_body: Hard qualifications carry the final 50 baseline points. Beyond that, a set of secondary signals separates candidates who score identically on the two questions above. Each moves someone by ten to twenty-five points, which is precisely the margin between rank 8 and rank 30. Six of them from this pool, with the candidate each one actually fired on:
rest_examples: Capsids she designed reached multiple external partner validations. Eighteen patent applications name her.
NSF Graduate Research Fellowship, Harvard BBS doctoral track, MIT computer science.
One record showing both generative modelling and hands-on mammalian cell culture, primary cell isolation and high-throughput screening.
Associate Director to Principal Scientist at Abiologics inside about six months.
Employed at Ampersand through the AbCheck acquisition.
Left Dyno after her doctoral affiliation, then returned as a Senior Scientist in 2025.
method.rest_close: Risk signals work the same way in the other direction. A pattern of consecutive short tenures, or a career spent entirely inside very large organisations with no small-company exposure, costs points rather than removing anybody. Nothing here is a filter. All of it is a ranking.

roster_intro: The full Elite band, ranked. The top ten are detailed in section 02 with the complete case for each. Below them, one line on why each person is on this list. The full written analysis for anybody here is available on request.

company: Nabla Bio is a Cambridge company, founded in 2020, that designs antibodies on a computer and then makes them and tests them in its own lab, in the same building, using the same people. AstraZeneca and Bristol Myers Squibb have signed research collaborations, and Takeda has signed two, the second in October 2025 with success payments that could pass a billion dollars.

Surge Biswas built the science in George Church's lab at Harvard, where he and his colleagues published some of the first work applying language models to proteins. He describes the model they built from it, JAM, as molecular auto-complete: give it a target and it completes the antibody that binds it, at the exact spot you asked for. Frances Anastassacos was one floor over in William Shih's lab, working on DNA origami. They met there. They are married.

The next year is about turning that into partnered programs. JAM-2 shipped in November 2025 across twenty-eight targets, and a 2026 report pushed it into T-cell engagers. There are about twenty-five people to do all of it.
role_narrative.role_heading: The role, and the hard part
role: Cambridge, MA. On site, five days a week.

In the first ninety days you take a real target and run a design campaign end to end. You pick the epitope, point JAM at it, decide with the wet-lab scientists what gets expressed and measured, and read what comes back. Then you tell the AI research team what the model got wrong.

Here is the hard part. About twenty-five people work here. There is no platform team to hand infrastructure to, no separate group to run your assay, and nobody standing between your model and the molecule. Nabla also publishes its technical reports in the open, and outside scientists picked apart the validation on the last one within weeks.
The payoff is the loop: design to data in two to three weeks. You find out fast whether you were right. The right person here has stopped waiting for someone else to run the experiment.
comp: Roughly $185,000 to $265,000 base against the 2026 Cambridge market, plus equity. The posting states salary, equity and benefits and publishes no figure.

must: Four or more years developing or applying AI in biology, chemistry or physics. Graduate and postdoctoral work counts in full.
Strong working Python, and real practice with a deep learning framework such as PyTorch.
Direct experience collaborating with wet-lab teams, or hands-on experimental work of their own.
Has personally decided what gets expressed and measured, rather than handing a model output to someone else.
preferred: Therapeutic experience, particularly antibodies or other protein drugs.
Familiarity with HPC environments such as Kubernetes or SLURM.
A doctorate in a quantitative field. The market norm and a strong signal.
Experience at a company under roughly 150 people where the same scientists owned both the model and the lab.
not_required: A doctorate. The posting asks for experience, not a degree, and we will not screen anyone out for its absence.
Antibody experience specifically. A generative design scientist on a different molecule class at a company your size transfers better than an antibody specialist inside a large pharma.
A senior title. Postdocs and staff scientists here routinely carry eight years of the required work.

channels: Two messages on one thread. The first names one specific reason we are writing to that person. The second is a reply with a different angle on the company and an offer to be pointed at someone else.
A live attempt, with a voicemail if unanswered. Roughly nine in ten hear the voicemail, which is why this carries the most weight.
Short, and the last one gives an easy way to say no. That courtesy is what gets replies.
Placed late rather than early. About one candidate in ten opens it, so it is for people who read nowhere else.
